1	# Maternal Mortality, Health Investment & Service Coverage: 8-Country Comparison
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	Four interrelated datasets track maternal mortality outcomes, health spending, skilled birth attendance, and rural-urban disparities across eight low- and middle-income countries (Ethiopia, India, Rwanda, Bangladesh, Nigeria, Cambodia, Peru, Nepal) from 2005 to 2021.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### maternal_mortality_timeseries
     9	- **Fields**: `country` (string, 8 values), `year` (integer, 2005/2009/2013/2017/2021), `mmr` (integer, deaths per 100,000 live births, range 69–946)
    10	- 40 rows total (8 countries × 5 time points)
    11	
    12	### health_expenditure_gdp
    13	- **Fields**: `country` (string), `year` (integer), `health_exp_pct_gdp` (float, % of GDP, range 2.4–8.2)
    14	- 40 rows, same country-year grid as mortality data
    15	
    16	### midwife_coverage
    17	- **Fields**: `country` (string), `period` (string, two survey windows: "2008-2012" and "2018-2021"), `skilled_birth_attendant_pct` (integer, % of births, range 10–95)
    18	- 16 rows (8 countries × 2 periods)
    19	
    20	### rural_urban_mmr_gap
    21	- **Fields**: `country` (string), `setting` ("urban" or "rural"), `mmr` (integer, deaths per 100,000 live births, range 38–860)
    22	- 16 rows (8 countries × 2 settings), representing latest estimates (~2019-2021)
    23	
    24	## Data Notes
    25	- MMR figures are modeled estimates aligned with WHO/UNICEF methodology; sub-national rural-urban splits are approximate.
    26	- Health expenditure includes both public and private spending.
    27	- Skilled birth attendant percentages are drawn from Demographic and Health Surveys and may not align exactly with the mortality time points.
    28	- Cambodia's MMR shows a reversal in 2021 reflecting reporting methodology changes.

1	# Mermaid.js Configuration & Theming
     2	
     3	Configuration options, theming, and customization for Mermaid.js v11.
     4	
     5	## Configuration Methods
     6	
     7	**1. Site-wide Initialization:**
     8	```javascript
     9	mermaid.initialize({
    10	  theme: 'dark',
    11	  startOnLoad: true,
    12	  securityLevel: 'strict',
    13	  fontFamily: 'Arial'
    14	});
    15	```
    16	
    17	**2. Diagram-level Frontmatter:**
    18	````markdown
    19	```mermaid
    20	---
    21	theme: forest
    22	look: handDrawn
    23	---
    24	flowchart TD
    25	  A --> B
    26	```
    27	````
    28	
    29	**3. Configuration Hierarchy:**
    30	Default config → Site config → Diagram config (highest priority)
    31	
    32	## Core Options
    33	
    34	**Rendering:**
    35	- `startOnLoad`: Auto-render on page load (default: true)
    36	- `securityLevel`: "strict" (default), "loose", "antiscript", "sandbox"
    37	- `deterministicIds`: Reproducible SVG IDs (default: false)
    38	- `maxTextSize`: Max diagram text (default: 50000)
    39	- `maxEdges`: Max drawable edges (default: 500)
    40	
    41	**Visual Style:**
    42	- `look`: "classic" (default), "handDrawn"
    43	- `handDrawnSeed`: Numeric seed for hand-drawn consistency
    44	- `darkMode`: Boolean toggle
    45	
    46	**Typography:**
    47	- `fontFamily`: "trebuchet ms, verdana, arial, sans-serif" (default)
    48	- `fontSize`: Base text size (default: 16)
    49	
    50	**Layout:**
    51	- `layout`: "dagre" (default), "elk", "tidy-tree", "cose-bilkent"
    52	
    53	**Debug:**
    54	- `logLevel`: 0-5 from trace to fatal
    55	- `htmlLabels`: Enable HTML in labels (default: false)
    56	
    57	## Theming
    58	
    59	**Built-in Themes:**
    60	- `default` - Standard colors
    61	- `dark` - Dark background
    62	- `forest` - Green tones
    63	- `neutral` - Grayscale
    64	- `base` - Fully customizable
    65	
    66	**Theme Variables (base theme only):**
    67	```javascript
    68	mermaid.initialize({
    69	  theme: 'base',
    70	  themeVariables: {
    71	    primaryColor: '#ff0000',
    72	    primaryTextColor: '#fff',
    73	    primaryBorderColor: '#7C0000',
    74	    secondaryColor: '#006100',
    75	    tertiaryColor: '#fff'
    76	  }
    77	});
    78	```
    79	
    80	**Customizable Variables:**
    81	- Color families: primary, secondary, tertiary
    82	- Node backgrounds and text colors
    83	- Border and line colors
    84	- Note background/text
    85	- Diagram-specific (flowchart nodes, sequence actors, pie sections)
    86	
    87	**Custom CSS:**
    88	```javascript
    89	mermaid.initialize({
    90	  themeCSS: `
    91	    .node rect { fill: #f9f; }
    92	    .edgeLabel { background-color: white; }
    93	  `
    94	});
    95	```
    96	
    97	## Accessibility
    98	
    99	**ARIA Support:**
   100	```
   101	accTitle: Diagram Title
   102	accDescr: Brief description
   103	accDescr {
   104	  Multi-line detailed
   105	  description
   106	}
   107	```
   108	
   109	**Auto-generated:**
   110	- `aria-roledescription` attributes
   111	- `<title>` and `<desc>` SVG elements
   112	- `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`
   113	
   114	**WCAG Compliance:**
   115	Available for all diagram types (flowchart, sequence, class, Gantt, etc.)
   116	
   117	## Icon Configuration
   118	
   119	**Register Icon Packs:**
   120	```javascript
   121	import { registerIconPacks } from 'mermaid';
   122	registerIconPacks([
   123	  {
   124	    name: 'logos',
   125	    loader: () => import('https://esm.run/@iconify-json/logos')
   126	  }
   127	]);
   128	```
   129	
   130	**Usage:**
   131	```
   132	architecture-beta
   133	  service api(logos:nodejs)[API]
   134	```
   135	
   136	**Loading Methods:**
   137	1. CDN-based (lazy loading)
   138	2. npm with dynamic import
   139	3. Direct import
   140	
   141	## Math Rendering
   142	
   143	**KaTeX Support:**
   144	```
   145	graph LR
   146	  A["$$f(x) = x^2$$"] --> B
   147	```
   148	
   149	**Configuration:**
   150	- `legacyMathML`: Use old MathML rendering
   151	- `forceLegacyMathML`: Force legacy even if browser supports native
   152	
   153	## Security
   154	
   155	**Security Levels:**
   156	- `strict` - HTML encoding (default, recommended)
   157	- `loose` - Some HTML allowed
   158	- `antiscript` - Filter scripts
   159	- `sandbox` - Sandboxed mode
   160	
   161	**DOMPurify:**
   162	Enabled by default for XSS protection. Customize via `dompurifyConfig` (use caution).
   163	
   164	## Layout Algorithms
   165	
   166	**dagre (default):**
   167	Standard hierarchical layout for most diagrams.
   168	
   169	**elk:**
   170	Advanced layout with better handling of complex graphs.
   171	
   172	**tidy-tree:**
   173	Clean tree structures for hierarchies.
   174	
   175	**cose-bilkent:**
   176	Compound graph layout for nested structures.
   177	
   178	**Per-diagram Configuration:**
   179	````markdown
   180	```mermaid
   181	---
   182	layout: elk
   183	---
   184	flowchart TD
   185	  A --> B
   186	```
   187	````
   188	
   189	## Common Patterns
   190	
   191	**Consistent Hand-drawn Style:**
   192	```javascript
   193	mermaid.initialize({
   194	  look: 'handDrawn',
   195	  handDrawnSeed: 42  // Same seed = consistent appearance
   196	});
   197	```
   198	
   199	**Dark Mode Toggle:**
   200	```javascript
   201	const isDark = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
   202	mermaid.initialize({
   203	  theme: isDark ? 'dark' : 'default'
   204	});
   205	```
   206	
   207	**Performance Optimization:**
   208	```javascript
   209	mermaid.initialize({
   210	  startOnLoad: false,  // Manual rendering
   211	  maxEdges: 1000,       // Increase for complex graphs
   212	  deterministicIds: true  // Caching-friendly
   213	});
   214	```

   218	**Parse without Rendering:**
   219	```javascript
   220	try {

import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.gridspec import GridSpec

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Color palette - professional, editorial, accessible
colors = {
    'Ethiopia': '#1f77b4',
    'India': '#ff7f0e',
    'Rwanda': '#2ca02c',
    'Bangladesh': '#d62728',
    'Nigeria': '#9467bd',
    'Cambodia': '#8c564b',
    'Peru': '#e377c2',
    'Nepal': '#7f7f7f',
}

# Prepare data structures
mmr_ts = {}
for row in data['maternal_mortality_timeseries']['data']:
    c = row['country']
    if c not in mmr_ts:
        mmr_ts[c] = {}
    mmr_ts[c][row['year']] = row['mmr']

exp_ts = {}
for row in data['health_expenditure_gdp']['data']:
    c = row['country']
    if c not in exp_ts:
        exp_ts[c] = {}
    exp_ts[c][row['year']] = row['health_exp_pct_gdp']

rural_urban = {}
for row in data['rural_urban_mmr_gap']['data']:
    c = row['country']
    if c not in rural_urban:
        rural_urban[c] = {}
    rural_urban[c][row['setting']] = row['mmr']

midwife = {}
for row in data['midwife_coverage']['data']:
    c = row['country']
    if c not in midwife:
        midwife[c] = {}
    midwife[c][row['period']] = row['skilled_birth_attendant_pct']

countries = list(colors.keys())
years = [2005, 2009, 2013, 2017, 2021]

# Calculate top improvers (% decline 2005-2021)
declines = {}
for c in countries:
    start = mmr_ts[c][2005]
    end = mmr_ts[c][2021]
    declines[c] = (start - end) / start * 100

top_improvers = sorted(declines.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)

# Create figure with custom layout
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18, 14), facecolor='white')
gs = GridSpec(2, 2, figure=fig, width_ratios=[1, 1], height_ratios=[1, 1], 
              wspace=0.28, hspace=0.32, left=0.07, right=0.93, top=0.92, bottom=0.08)

# ---- Panel 1: MMR Trends over Time (top-left) ----
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
for c in countries:
    vals = [mmr_ts[c][y] for y in years]
    linewidth = 3.0 if declines[c] > 65 else 1.8
    alpha = 1.0 if declines[c] > 65 else 0.7
    zorder = 5 if declines[c] > 65 else 3
    ax1.plot(years, vals, color=colors[c], linewidth=linewidth, alpha=alpha, 
             marker='o', markersize=5 if declines[c] > 65 else 4, zorder=zorder, label=c)

# Highlight top improvers with annotations
for c, pct in top_improvers[:3]:
    ax1.annotate(f'{c}\n(-{pct:.0f}%)', 
                 xy=(2021, mmr_ts[c][2021]), 
                 xytext=(2022.5, mmr_ts[c][2021]),
                 fontsize=9, color=colors[c], fontweight='bold',
                 arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=colors[c], lw=1.2))

ax1.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_ylabel('Maternal Mortality Ratio\n(deaths per 100,000 live births)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_title('A. Maternal Mortality Decline (2005–2021)', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', loc='left')
ax1.set_xticks(years)
ax1.set_xlim(2004, 2025)
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')
ax1.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax1.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# ---- Panel 2: Health Expenditure % GDP (top-right) ----
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
for c in countries:
    vals = [exp_ts[c][y] for y in years]
    linewidth = 3.0 if declines[c] > 65 else 1.8
    alpha = 1.0 if declines[c] > 65 else 0.7
    zorder = 5 if declines[c] > 65 else 3
    ax2.plot(years, vals, color=colors[c], linewidth=linewidth, alpha=alpha,
             marker='s', markersize=5 if declines[c] > 65 else 4, zorder=zorder)

# Annotate Rwanda (high spender, high improver) and Nigeria (low improver)
ax2.annotate('Rwanda\n(highest spender)', xy=(2021, exp_ts['Rwanda'][2021]), 
             xytext=(2015, 8.8), fontsize=9, color=colors['Rwanda'], fontweight='bold',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=colors['Rwanda'], lw=1.2))
ax2.annotate('Nigeria\n(slowest decline)', xy=(2021, exp_ts['Nigeria'][2021]), 
             xytext=(2016.5, 2.0), fontsize=9, color=colors['Nigeria'], fontweight='bold',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=colors['Nigeria'], lw=1.2))

ax2.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_ylabel('Health Expenditure (% of GDP)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_title('B. Health Expenditure Trajectory (% of GDP)', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', loc='left')
ax2.set_xticks(years)
ax2.set_xlim(2004, 2025)
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')
ax2.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax2.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# ---- Panel 3: Rural-Urban Disparity (bottom-left) ----
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
x = np.arange(len(countries))
width = 0.35
urban_vals = [rural_urban[c]['urban'] for c in countries]
rural_vals = [rural_urban[c]['rural'] for c in countries]
gaps = [rural_vals[i] - urban_vals[i] for i in range(len(countries))]

bars1 = ax3.bar(x - width/2, urban_vals, width, label='Urban', color='#5B9BD5', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)
bars2 = ax3.bar(x + width/2, rural_vals, width, label='Rural', color='#C55A11', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)

# Add gap annotations
for i, (u, r, g) in enumerate(zip(urban_vals, rural_vals, gaps)):
    ax3.annotate(f'+{g}', xy=(x[i], r + 15), ha='center', fontsize=8, 
                 color='#333333', fontweight='bold')

ax3.set_xlabel('Country', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_ylabel('Maternal Mortality Ratio\n(deaths per 100,000 live births)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_title('C. Rural–Urban Disparity (Latest Estimate, ~2019–2021)', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', loc='left')
ax3.set_xticks(x)
ax3.set_xticklabels(countries, rotation=30, ha='right', fontsize=10)
ax3.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True, fancybox=False, edgecolor='#cccccc')
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--', axis='y')
ax3.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax3.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# ---- Panel 4: Midwife Coverage vs MMR 2021 (bottom-right) ----
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
midwife_latest = [midwife[c]['2018-2021'] for c in countries]
mmr_2021 = [mmr_ts[c][2021] for c in countries]
coverage_change = [midwife[c]['2018-2021'] - midwife[c]['2008-2012'] for c in countries]

# Bubble sizes proportional to coverage change
sizes = [max(80, c * 12) for c in coverage_change]

for i, c in enumerate(countries):
    ax4.scatter(midwife_latest[i], mmr_2021[i], s=sizes[i], color=colors[c], 
                alpha=0.75, edgecolors='white', linewidth=1.5, zorder=5)
    # Offset labels to avoid overlap
    offset_x = 2
    offset_y = 8 if i % 2 == 0 else -18
    ax4.annotate(c, (midwife_latest[i] + offset_x, mmr_2021[i] + offset_y), 
                 fontsize=9, color=colors[c], fontweight='bold')

# Trend line
z = np.polyfit(midwife_latest, mmr_2021, 1)
p = np.poly1d(z)
x_line = np.linspace(min(midwife_latest)-5, max(midwife_latest)+5, 100)
ax4.plot(x_line, p(x_line), '--', color='#666666', alpha=0.6, linewidth=1.5, label='Trend')

ax4.set_xlabel('Skilled Birth Attendant Coverage (% of births, 2018–2021)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_ylabel('Maternal Mortality Ratio 2021\n(deaths per 100,000 live births)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_title('D. Skilled Birth Attendance vs. Maternal Mortality', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', loc='left')
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')
ax4.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax4.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# Bubble size legend
legend_sizes = [20, 40]
legend_bubbles = []
for s in legend_sizes:
    legend_bubbles.append(ax4.scatter([], [], s=max(80, s*12), c='#999999', alpha=0.6, edgecolors='white'))
ax4.legend(legend_bubbles, ['+20pp coverage', '+40pp coverage'], 
           title='Coverage gain\n(2008–2012 to 2018–2021)', 
           loc='upper right', frameon=True, fancybox=False, edgecolor='#cccccc', fontsize=8)

# Overall title
fig.suptitle('Maternal Mortality, Health Investment & Service Coverage: 8-Country Comparison (2005–2021)', 
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.97)

# Color legend for countries (placed in the center between top panels)
legend_patches = [mpatches.Patch(color=colors[c], label=c) for c in countries]
fig.legend(handles=legend_patches, loc='upper center', bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.92),
           ncol=8, frameon=False, fontsize=10, columnspacing=1.5)

# Source note
fig.text(0.07, 0.02, 
         'Data sources: WHO/UNICEF maternal mortality estimates; World Bank health expenditure; DHS skilled birth attendance. '
         'Cambodia 2021 MMR reflects reporting methodology changes.',
         fontsize=9, color='#666666', style='italic')

plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=200, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
print("Chart saved to /app/output/result.png")
